title: Raspberry Curd
subtitle: Sharp, jewel-pink curd made with fresh raspberries
excerpt: Raspberry curd is made the same way as lemon curd, eggs, butter, sugar, but the raspberry juice replaces the lemon. Sharp, vivid pink, and best eaten within 3 weeks. Makes two small jars.
sourceNotes: Pam Corbin, Preserves. Fruit curds made with berry juices require straining to remove seeds and pulp before the eggs are added.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge and stir before using.

glossaryTerms.definition: A heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, so the steam heats the bowl gently. Used for delicate emulsions like curd and custard where direct heat would scramble the eggs.

content.text: Raspberry curd has the same rich, egg-and-butter base as lemon curd, but the sharpness comes from raspberry juice rather than lemon. The colour is a deep, jewel pink. It sets softly,  raspberries have less acidity to firm the eggs than lemon does,  so it works best as a filling or spread rather than a firm set curd. Makes about two 200 g jars.

items.prepNote: to sharpen and help the set

content.text: Put the raspberries in a small saucepan with a splash of water and warm over low heat until they collapse and release their juice, about 5 minutes. Press through a fine sieve into a bowl, pushing firmly to extract as much juice as possible. Discard the seeds and skin. You need about 100 to 120 ml of juice.
Put the raspberry juice, lemon juice, sugar, and butter in a heatproof

a pan of barely simmering water. Stir until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves. Add the beaten eggs and stir constantly for 15 to 20 minutes until the curd thickens enough to coat a spoon. Keep the water at a low simmer throughout,  the eggs will scramble over high heat.
Pour through a fine sieve into hot sterilised jars. Seal and cool. The curd thickens further as it cools.

items.cause: Berry curds set softer than lemon curd, this is normal.
items.fix: Add an extra yolk next time, or use 2 tbsp lemon juice to increase acidity. Raspberry curd will never be as firm as lemon curd.

items.cause: Overheated, the raspberry pigments are sensitive to prolonged heat.
items.fix: Keep the water at a bare simmer and don't rush the cooking time. The colour remains bright when cooked gently.

items.cause: Sieve was not fine enough or not pressed through properly.
items.fix: Pass through a fine-mesh sieve a second time. A fine nylon sieve works better than metal for removing all seeds.

items.cause: Raspberry flavour is mild once cooked with butter and sugar.
items.fix: Add 1 tsp of raspberry extract or stir in a few crushed fresh raspberries at the end, just before jarring.

content.text: Refrigerate immediately. Use within 3 weeks. Freezes for up to 3 months.
